solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Saw nothing untoward in Irving

indicators.note: untoward means awkward or out of order, so the letters of the two words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reading the stories of Irving finds nothing improper in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington Irving was the American author of Rip Van Winkle, so his first name is defined by the surname that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer's full name was Washington Irving, so his forename partners the surname given in the clue.

clue.text: One Direction, lifeless boy band?

indicators.note: lifeless here says the band's name is left without the word life at its end

parts.note: Westlife was an Irish boy band of the 1990s and 2000s

explanation.surface: One Direction, the pop group, is mocked as a dull boy band without any spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' looks like the boy band itself, but it is the definition: one compass point. Westlife is an Irish boy band.
explanation.definitionFit: West is one of the four compass points, so it is a single direction.

clue.text: Exhibit pig fed by husband

indicators.note: fed by means the word for pig takes the husband's letter into itself

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A prize pig on display at an agricultural fair is fed by the farmer's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to display it publicly, and a show is a display.

clue.text: Poor devil above, one stuck on top of outhouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck on top of puts one piece directly above the next

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
over means above
I is the Roman numeral one
a shed is an outhouse

explanation.surface: A poor little devil is perched on the roof of an outdoor shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impoverished has been made poor, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Short reptile, silver, turned up on hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A silvery reptile is spotted lying upturned on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a shortened, informal form of alligator, which is a reptile.

clue.text: Preparation of belladonna, but not at first for everybody

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up from ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new arrangement
not tells us a letter is to be left out of belladonna
at first takes the opening letter of the word but

explanation.surface: A medicine made from belladonna is offered, though not at first, to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not at first' means remove the first letter of 'but', B, from BELLADONNA, leaving ELLADONNA, which 'Preparation of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning every single person, the whole lot of them together.

clue.text: Clue would be perfect, if shortened

indicators.note: if shortened says the word for perfect loses its final letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A setter muses that a crossword clue would be perfect if only it were trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue can mean a notion or inkling, as in 'I haven't a clue', which is a synonym.

clue.text: Outrageous, a local bid, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone suspects that a bid made by a local is scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolical is used informally for something appallingly bad or shocking, much the same as outrageous.

clue.text: A grant, finally — cash available for immediate use

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of grant

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A grant has at last come through, giving cash to spend straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the ready is prepared and to hand, so it can be used immediately.

clue.text: Athlete's attempt with golf club

definitions.note: read as 'Athlete is', with the 's standing for is

parts.note: a shot is an attempt
a putter is a golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A sportsman takes a swing with a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in the field event of hurling the heavy ball is an athlete.

clue.text: Mould in shed

definitions.meaning: a mould for ... metal, or something formed in it
to shed is to throw off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: Mould is growing inside a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a mould or the shape made in one, and a snake casts off its skin, sheds it.

clue.text: Complete discretion in tabernacle abroad? Check inside

indicators.note: inside puts the check abbreviation within the rearranged letters
abroad means widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A priest asks whether one has free rein in a foreign tabernacle, and checks inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' gives CARTEBLANE, and 'inside' places the chess shorthand within it, just before the final E. 'Complete discretion' is the French phrase's usual English gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche, French for a blank paper, means full freedom to act as one sees fit.

clue.text: In addition, finished a short book about food fish

parts.note: something over is finished or ended

indicators.note: about means the shortened book goes around the fish
short says the word for book loses its last letter

parts.note: a novel is a book
a dab is a small flatfish eaten as food

explanation.surface: Having finished a brief book, someone reads more about edible fish as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' leaves NOVE, and 'about' gives NDABOVE; 'food fish' is a flatfish, not a general term for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means besides or extra, in excess of what is required, hence in addition.

clue.text: Look at belt and a sort of band one may wear on one's wrist

definitions.text: a sort of band one may wear on one's wrist

parts.note: to watch is to look at
a strap is a belt

explanation.surface: Someone compares a belt with a wristband they might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of leather or metal that holds a timepiece to the arm is this kind of band.

clue.text: Paid seller anyway for just one sandal!

indicators.note: anyway read as 'in any way' suggests the letters can go in any order

explanation.surface: A seller is paid in full, but only one sandal of the pair is handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just one' is there because the shoes are usually sold and named as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rope-soled canvas shoe, a kind of summer sandal, given here in the singular.

clue.text: Film of a lake in European country

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the name of the country

parts.note: Austria is a country in central Europe

explanation.surface: A movie is filmed at a lake in some European country.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the 2008 Baz Luhrmann film starring Nicole Kidman and Hugh Jackman.
explanation.definitionFit: The epic movie by Baz Luhrmann bears the continent's name as its title.

clue.text: One who'll help if several in distress

indicators.note: distress suggests disorder or damage, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone promises to help if several people get into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer who saves a drowning swimmer is a person who comes to help.

clue.text: Food in centre of canteen, ready to eat

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letter of canteen

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Food in the middle of the canteen is ready for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe, the stomach lining of a cow, is a traditional British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal eaten as food, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Form C girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl belongs to form C at school.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class of pupils, often labelled by a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A school form is a group of pupils taught together, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Rich directors making a deal in a hotel?

parts.note: a rich flavour is full
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Wealthy company directors strike a business deal while staying at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a business deal, but it means a hotel package.
explanation.definitionFit: Full board is a hotel arrangement that includes all meals, an accommodation package.

clue.text: Far superior thoroughfare's coming up

parts.note: a street is a thoroughfare, with the 's attached
something coming up lies ahead

explanation.surface: A road sign warns that a main road is approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom describes something much better than its rivals, way out in front.

clue.text: Grating last of Cheddar into mince

indicators.note: into puts the single letter inside the word for mince

parts.note: hash is a dish of minced or chopped meat

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of Cheddar

explanation.surface: A cook grates the end of the Cheddar into minced meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating sound is rough and unpleasant, which is what harsh means.

clue.text: Powder in metal container

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Powder is kept in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for the skin.

clue.text: Shock caused by dangerous feat? No end

indicators.note: no end means the word for the feat loses its last letter

parts.note: a stunt is a dangerous feat, as by a stuntman

explanation.surface: Onlookers are shocked by an endlessly risky feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' looks like the phrase meaning 'a great deal', but here it removes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to shock or astonish someone.

clue.text: Function of burger bun, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is to be pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a bread roll holds a burger

explanation.surface: Someone asks what job a burger bun actually does.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is a function or job, the part something plays.

clue.text: A victory so unusual for this country, in the past

indicators.note: unusual says the letters are found in an odd order

explanation.surface: A rare victory for some country long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the past' because the West African country now officially uses the French name Côte d'Ivoire.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the English name used for the West African nation now officially called Côte d'Ivoire.

clue.text: Look one way, then the other

indicators.note: one way then the other says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone checks left then right, as if crossing a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick look or glance.

clue.text: Charade used to trick ecclesiastical dignitary

indicators.note: used means worked over or handled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A game of charades is used to fool a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican cleric ranking below a bishop, a church dignitary.
